blogs.title: The 0.5mg Rule: Why Weight-Based Epinephrine Dosing Matters in Adult Anaphylaxis
blogs.description: A deep dive into epinephrine dosing controversies, analyzing the case of a 104kg patient treated with 0.3mg auto-injectors versus the recommended 0.01mg/kg (max 0.5mg). We discuss the risks of underdosing in heavy adults and the evidence supporting higher initial doses in severe anaphylaxis.

blogs.title: To Steroid or Not to Steroid? The Fading Role of Corticosteroids in Anaphylaxis
blogs.description: Reviewing the evidence behind the traditional use of corticosteroids to prevent biphasic reactions. We contrast the case patient's treatment with recent systematic reviews showing no benefit and potential harm, guiding clinicians on when (or if) to break the dogma.

blogs.title: When to Discharge? Risk Stratification and Observation Times for Biphasic Anaphylaxis
blogs.description: Addressing the critical question of observation duration after symptom resolution. We explore the debate between standard 4-6 hour monitoring versus extended observation for high-risk patients, using the multiphasic course of this case to illustrate the dangers of premature discharge.

blogs.title: The Silent Underlayer: Clinical Clues for Systemic Mastocytosis in Severe Anaphylaxis
blogs.description: How to recognize when anaphylaxis might be a symptom of an underlying mast cell disorder. We highlight non-allergic clues from the case, such as hepatomegaly and neuropsychiatric symptoms, and discuss the importance of suspecting mastocytosis in recurrent or severe episodes.

blogs.title: The Tryptase Timing Trap: Diagnostic Pitfalls in Acute Anaphylaxis Workup
blogs.description: A practical guide to the correct timing of tryptase sampling (acute vs. baseline) to diagnose mast cell disorders. We analyze the missed diagnostic opportunity in this case due to delayed sampling and provide a protocol for optimal tryptase evaluation in the ED.

blogs.title: Biphasic, Refractory, or Sustained? Defining the Course to Guide Management
blogs.description: Clarifying the often-confused terminology of complex anaphylaxis courses. We distinguish between true biphasic reactions, refractory anaphylaxis, and sustained symptoms, and explain how accurate classification dictates ICU admission and escalation of therapy.
